Compared to the traditional "corner-sewn" elastics found in most traditional fitted sheets, the bands in this sheet set help keep it firmly in place.

One especially nice feature of all of Slumber Cloud's bedding: it offers a 30-night trial for purchases made directly from the brand.

Industry observers note that if you’re an extra-hot sleeper, however, you may want to look elsewhere. While Wilkinson found these sheets cooling, she says that, despite claims about being designed with “NASA cooling technology,” they didn’t seem to cool her off better than her previous sheet set. Still, they are great at wicking moisture and are incredibly durable.

(Pro tip: The Performance Sheet Set is, in our opinion, Slumber Cloud's best cooling sheet set. But, if you're looking for almost-as-good performance with a classic sheet feel, opt for its Essential Sheet Set which blends cotton with Outlast fibers.).

Sources indicate that if you love the silky smoothness of cotton sateen sheets, Sijo’s AiryWeight Eucalyptus Sheets offer a similar feel while being 70 percent more moisture-absorbing. Made with naturally hypoallergenic Tencel Lyocell, the glossy silk-like texture of the sheets is a great option for those with sensitive skin, especially if certain materials make you feel itchy. Plus, the set boasts OEKO-TEX and Asthma and Allergy Friendly certifications.

“The feel of these are incredible,” says WH fitness editor Cori Ritchey. “With cooling sheets, I tend to fear they're going to be too slick and not cozy. These are kind of the perfect blend.” The sheets feel silky but not slippery, she adds.

In a recent development, at $185 for a queen-size set, these Sijo sheets aren’t cheap, but they are long lasting. The brand claims the sheets survived 2,000 rubs without pilling in lab testing. They passed Ritchey’s personal durability test, too: “They wash very nicely—they don't seem to lose their texture the longer you use them,” she notes. And for those of us whose top sheet ends up on the floor most nights, you can subtract the flat sheet from the set for a $75 discount.

Recent findings suggest that one of the downsides of the sheets is the two-month return window that only applies if the bedding is unopened—but there is a catch here. Sijo offers a 30-night bedding trial for eligible direct purchases. Return-shipping charges depend on whether you purchased Checkout+, so check the terms before ordering. Some customers have also noted that the sheets shrink a little after the first wash (we didn’t notice this during testing, but it’s worth flagging).

Some hot sleepers merely need sheets that are breathable throughout the night, while others prefer bedding that is immediately cool to the touch. If you want a set of sheets that feels like sleeping on the cool side of the pillow all night long, Sijo’s AiryWeight Eucalyptus Sheets are for you. “I'm normally a hot sleeper and these have kept me cool and comfortable,” Ritchey says.

Linen sheets are a great option for hot sleepers, if you’re willing to spend a little more. Brooklinen’s Linen Core Sheets are made with 100 percent European flax that softens with each wash, although they may be a little rough for sensitive skin right out of the box. The sheets are breathable yet they have a weight to them, which makes them great for year-round use.

“These sheets are so soft and cozy—truly the most comfortable material I have ever slept on,” claims WH associate editor Olivia Luppino. “I actively look forward to getting into bed with them.” She describes the sheets as plush to the touch, while still maintaining a sleekness that gives them a cooling feel. “They definitely keep me cool in warm summer months,” she says. “I’m very into these sheets.”.

That said, one of the (few) downsides is the $300-plus price tag, which is expensive but not outrageous when it comes to linen sheets. Plus, Brooklinen tends to run frequent sales, so it’s not unusual to see a 25 percent discount. The sheets have gotten softer with each wash, but at the same time they wear like iron with no snagging, pulling, or pilling to be found.

They are also OEKO-TEX certified and come with the longest return window of our favorite cooling sheets at a whopping 365 days. If you’re looking to make an investment that will last and keep you cool in any climate, Brooklinen’s Linen Core Sheets are worth the splurge.

Sources indicate that to curate a list of the best cooling sheets, we recruited eight Women's Health staffers to personally vet a wide range of sets in various temperatures and environments over the past year. For instance, we slept in Casper's Hyperlite Sheet Set in July with no air-conditioning, glamped with Mellanni's Iconic Collection in Newly introduced Hampshire, and cozied up in SlumberCloud's Performance Sheet Set with the window open in 80-degree heat “for science.” Then, our testing editors narrowed the selections by evaluating each sheet set based on style, fit, price point, comfort, breathability, moisture management, softness, durability after washing, wrinkling or pilling, and value.

It probably goes without saying that sheet material matters above all else. Natural fibers, like linen and cotton, are often best, according to Brager. They tend to be more breathable and absorbent (more on why that's actually a good thing below) than others, which means they won't trap heat that can make you sweat as you catch your Z's.

Your sheets’ weave is the pattern used to hold the threads together to make the fabric. Percale is generally considered the best weave for hot sleepers. This type of weave uses a simple pattern that maximizes airflow and has a lightweight feel, lowering the odds it will trap body heat while you snooze.

It’s generally recommended that you avoid sateen or flannel sheets if you’re looking for a cooling feel. These tend to be denser and hold onto heat as a result.

There are so many factors that go into how cool you feel when you slip between the sheets at night, including the temperature of your room, your body temperature, the weight of your comforter, and your mattress composition. But we sweat a lot throughout the night. "If you don't have something that's absorbent, you will marinate in sweat," Young says. That's why natural materials that are highly absorbent, like linen and cotton, are notable. "Even more important than that is wicking, which means getting moisture to the surface for evaporation," says Young. The two of these features working in tandem is what keeps you both dry and cool.

Sources indicate that moisture-wicking sheets can be one element to help keep you cool at night. These sheets are specially designed to pull moisture away from your skin and evaporate, allowing you to feel cooler, faster. They also tend to feel a little airier than other sheets.

In a recent development, that doesn’t mean you won’t ever feel hot if you use moisture-wicking sheets—again, there’s a lot happening when you sleep that can influence your body’s temperature. But you can usually feel a difference between how you feel when using moisture-wicking sheets and other types of sheets.

Industry observers note that beyond the material of your cooling sheets, the quality of that material is key. Back in the day, thread count was the single most important measure of quality in bedding. Anything above 600-thread-count was often considered good, while 800 and above was downright luxurious. But advances in technology have allowed us to create sheets with a 1,500, even 2,000, thread count. That’s not necessarily a good thing, as that figure can be inflated and used as a marketing gimmick.

According to recent reports, plus, super-high thread-count sheets usually aren’t all they're cracked up to be. “My experience with those is that they’re not strong, and they don’t hold up well,” indicates Deborah Young, owner of TheTextileExpert.com and a clinical assistant professor of textiles at Arizona State University. “They are seductively soft, but for me, there’s a point of diminishing returns.”.

Thread count can be a measure of quality, but you'll want to consider other factors, too, especially when shopping for the best cooling sheets. Some manufacturers rely on GSM (or grams per square meter) as this is a measure of weight rather than thread density.

Young's most important tip for hot sleepers, however, is that they may actually benefit from sheets with a lower thread count (like 400). A higher thread count often means the sheets are denser, offering better coverage, but a hot sleeper would probably want to avoid this.

It depends. Every brand we recommend below offers a return policy with a minimum 30-day term. Some, however, only accept returns for unopened sheet sets in the original packaging. Others provide longer terms (up to 365 days) with no questions asked, effectively like a free in-home trial.

There are a variety of certifications out there to ensure that consumers are getting high-quality bedding and textiles. One of the most common labels you’ll find on sheets is the OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification, which means that the product has been tested for more than 1,000 harmful substances. Some sheets may also have sustainability labels, like FSC certification, or an Asthma & Allergy Friendly certification from the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America. Keep in mind that more certifications tend to lead to a higher price tag, though—and not all are necessary.

According to recent reports, our favorite cooling sheets range in price from $37 to $322 for a queen-size set. There’s no need to spend hundreds on a set of sheets—you can easily find high-quality cooling sheets for $100-plus. However, certain fabrics like linen will cost more and in return should survive many years of use.

In a recent development, women’s Health first wrote this story in 2019 and has been continuously testing latest cooling sheets as they’re released. During that time, some clear favorites have emerged. For this patch, we had several WH staffers and contributors test these products in their own beds. Each sheet set was tested for two to three weeks or longer, and evaluated on their cooling abilities, softness, and durability, among other factors. Testers ranged from those who regularly wake up sweaty to people who consider themselves “neutral” in terms of sleep temperature.

Yes, cooling sheets actually work. They’re designed to be lightweight, breathable, and moisture-wicking, all of which can make you feel cooler when you sleep at night. However, there are a lot of factors that influence how hot you feel at night, including the type of mattress and comforter you have. Ultimately, cooling sheets are one more way to help you feel comfortable, but they shouldn’t be the only thing you use if you tend to run hot while you sleep.

Cotton is usually considered best, but you have a few options to choose from when it comes to cooling materials for sheets.

Bamboo sheets can be cooler than cotton sheets, but that’s not always the case. The weave of your sheets matters. A cotton percale weave sheet can be very cooling and even more cooling than standard bamboo sheets. But cotton is also used to make flannel sheets—which are heat-insulating, not cooling—making it hard to rely on fabric alone when choosing the best cooling sheets.

Thread count is usually linked to the softness of sheets, but it can impact how cool sheets feel. A higher thread count typically means that sheets are denser, which can work against your efforts to stay cool. That’s why Young suggests choosing sheets with a lower thread count, like 400, over much higher thread count options.

According to recent reports, cooling sheets should be washed as often as “regular” sheets, which means they should be washed every week, notes Kelly Murray, a certified pediatric and adult sleep coach in Chicago. This will allow you to wash away any allergens, keeping your sheets feeling crisp and fresh, she adds.

Recent findings suggest that by the way, you should wash your cooling sheets before using them, too. "You're washing off any dust the sheets may have collected in the warehouse, which can irritate your respiratory system and lead to sleep issues,” Murray notes.

Some cooling sheets, especially those made with natural fibers like cotton and linen, soften with each successive wash. If your fresh set feels a little too stiff or "crunchy," try running them through a machine wash cycle or two to soften them.

There is an almost universal rule among experts that you should be changing your sheets every week, and Murray concurs. If you don't want to wash your sheets that often, you should consider purchasing an extra set to swap out each week.

As for when it's time to swap out cooling sheets for brand new ones, that's up to you. Murray says she purchases a new set whenever she sees them on sale, but recommends replacing yours about every two to three years.

Industry observers note that ICYDK, your body temperature needs to drop about 2 degrees lower at night in order to synthesize melatonin, Murray indicates. So, it is super important that you create an environment that allows for this. That means ensuring your bedroom is "dark, cool, and quiet" when you're ready for bed.

Recent findings suggest that other than investing in some cooling sheets, you can also improve your sleep quality by keeping a consistent sleep routine that involves ending screen time at least an hour before you go to bed. "Your body and brain are always looking for patterns throughout the day to know what happens next," Murray says. "So if you have a consistent bedtime routine that's very relaxing, that will trigger the production of melatonin and help your brain to unwind.".

GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

In a recent development, GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

Recent findings suggest that chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate plan, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

An EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

Recent findings suggest that not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

According to recent reports, GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the newly introduced-for-2026 Ferrari 296 Speciale is a sharper, faster, and more track-oriented variant of the brand’s V-6 supercar—but that doesn’t mean it is the only high-performance variant of the car that Ferrari will build. In a somewhat surprising break from recent tradition, Ferrari is also going to make a Challenge Stradale variant of the 296 to sell alongside the Speciale.

Industry observers note that as the name suggests, the Challenge Stradale is a road-going variant of the 296 that shares a lot in common with the race car currently used in various Ferrari Challenge series. Specifically, its aerodynamic elements are strikingly similar to the fresh 296 Challenge Evo, which was revealed alongside the new road car on November 21. The massive rear wing, front dive planes, and aggressive rear splitter are all extremely similar to design elements seen on that race car.

Those components combine to create a massive 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 miles per hour, an increase of 72 percent over the 296 GTB that won Road & Track Performance Car of the Year in 2024. Downforce is also up 401 lbs at that speed on the 296 Speciale, an increase of 29 percent.

The removal of the hybrid system means a reduction in power, dropping from a combined system output of 819 horsepower in the 296 GTB to an engine-only output of 670 hp in the Challenge Stradale. The simplified powertrain and stripped out interior mean serious reductions in weight to match, though; the Challenge Stradale is 309 lbs lighter than the GTB and 176 lbs lighter than the Speciale.

Industry observers note that does the reduction in weight and increase in downforce make the 296 Challenge Stradale faster than the hybrid 296 Speciale already on the market? Not necessarily. Ferrari claims the Challenge Stradale is half a second a lap faster at its Fiorano test track, but marginally slower at a high-speed circuit like Monza. The more powerful Speciale should be quicker on other tracks with the on-throttle time necessary to allow the hybrid to stretch its legs, while the lighter Challenge Stradale should have the advantage on more technical circuits with more off-throttle time.

According to recent reports, the other major differentiation between the Speciale and the Challenge Stradale is availability. While that other high-end 296 variant was a limited-run model, Ferrari stresses that the Challenge Stradale is a part of its regular lineup, and should be more available to buyers. It remains a Ferrari, so the market is unlikely to be flooded with 296s with massive wings in the years to come, but by supercar standards, it should be relatively attainable.

Sources indicate that ferrari has not yet announced a price for the American market, but the brand claims that it should start at the equivalent of just under $320,000 in Italy, including value-added tax. Prices in one region do not necessarily translate directly to another, but that number would leave the 296 Challenge Stradale in the general range of the similarly track-focused likes of Porsche’s 911 GT3 RS and Ford’s Mustang GTD.

According to recent reports, the Volkswagen GTI badge has been a staple in automotive culture for 50 years, and it’s clearly not getting sidelined anytime soon. VW just released the ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept, an electric track-focused GTI that slots in as the automaker’s fourth latest GTI variant this year.

In a recent development, while it’s not heading to production, the Clubsport concept is a peek into the possibilities riding on the electric ID.Polo GTI, which became the first EV to wear the GTI badge when it was released earlier this year. The standard ID.Polo GTI, which isn’t sold in the United States, reaches 62 mph in 6.8 seconds thanks to a 223-hp electric motor mounted to the front axle.

See all results for Volkswagen ID.GTI for sale near 20147.

It has been revealed that the Clubsport concept ups the ante, with VW claiming it will hit 62 mph in just 4.7 seconds with the help of launch control and a more powerful APP550 electric motor. The upgraded motor, which is typically used to power the rear wheels of larger models like the ID.Tiguan and ID.7, sends 362 horsepower to the front wheels and nearly doubles the standard electric GTI’s torque output from 213 to 406 pound-feet.

Sources indicate that volkswagen also equipped the concept vehicle with an electronically regulated front differential lock, a performance-tuned adaptive suspension system, and ceramic brakes with a one-box brake setup. The high-performance powertrain fits into an equally aggressive two-door build, complete with a large front splitter, diffuser, and a flared rear wing.

It has been revealed that rather than the typical five-seater setup, the Clubsport concept houses two Recaro bucket seats with red five-point harnesses. A Tornado Red roll bar replaces the rear seats, and the cockpit is solely reserved for racing needs, meaning the standard infotainment system is also omitted. The cabin is finished in a dark microfiber material and trimmed with red stitching.

According to recent reports, volkswagen calls this concept the “perfect match of heritage and future,” and the automaker says its young employees were involved in much of the concept’s realization. The ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept won’t ever make it to VW showrooms, but it’ll be displayed next week at the Essen Motor Show in Essen, Germany.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s pretty clear at this stage that Arc Raiders is one of the biggest introduces of 2025. More interesting than the numbers themselves, however, is that this is an extraction shooter - a subgenre which has typically been thought of as niche.

If you’ve been paying the PvPvE game any attention, you could easily see how (and why) it keeps breaking its own records.

Today, publisher Nexon unveiled in a press release (via Gematsu) that Arc Raiders has now sold over 4 million copies. The game came out on October 30, which means it managed to sell that many copies in a little over 10 days.

The news comes on the same day that developer Embark Studios confirmed that the game had more than 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms over the weekend. Over the same weekend on Steam alone, Arc Raiders broke its own Steam concurrent record with a new peak of 462,488 players - which is a significant chunk of that 700,000+ player base.

This marks the second time the extraction shooter has broken its own concurrent player records, which is something very few games have managed in the past. Arc Raiders remains a top-seller, too. On Steam, it’s presently the second-best seller globally (by revenue), sitting just below Counter-Strike 2.

“The many different ways you play and participate in ARC Raiders have completely blown us away, going far beyond what we ever imagined. You surprise us, you outsmart us, and you keep us on our toes. We wouldn’t have it any other way,” the developer wrote on Twitter.

Embark recently published a roadmap to highlight all the latest content coming to the game over the remainder of this year. The first new map is set to arrive this month alongside new Arc units, new gameplay items, new events and more.

Industry observers note that just over the weekend, the game received several new Map Conditions that completely alter the way they play. The developer has already rolled out a couple of updates since launch, in order to tackle exploits and fix a few launchday bugs.

If you’re currently hooked on this gem of a game, we guarantee that our Arc Raiders gameplay tips will have at least one you didn’t know about. We also have more guides on how to find some of the more elusive items in the game, such as olives, lemons and apricots, and prickly pears.

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-new, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

Recent findings suggest that for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s new NTE240E is different, representing a company’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

Let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so major a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

Plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s new dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

Industry observers note that the combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

According to recent reports, that efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL says each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

It has been revealed that what’s more, because the substantial BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the new NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

Why Cancer Biomarker Testing Is Personal for Mark-Paul Gosselaar

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Known for his iconic roles on “Saved by the Bell,” “NYPD Blue,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Found,” Mark-Paul Gosselaar knows how to grab an audience.
  • Now, he’s using that star power to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing while sharing how he prioritizes his own health and well-being.
  • “Health is a huge thing for my wife and I, and our family,” Gosselaar told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Known for his iconic roles on “Saved by the Bell,” “NYPD Blue,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Found,” Mark-Paul Gosselaar knows how to grab an audience.

Now, he’s using that star power to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing while sharing how he prioritizes his own health and well-being.

“Health is a huge thing for my wife and I, and our family,” Gosselaar told Healthline. “We are constantly aware of new technologies.”.

Having seen people in his life navigate cancer diagnoses, Gosselaar is now raising awareness about the role of biomarker testing in cancer treatment through his partnership with AstraZeneca and its Meet Your Mark campaign.

The campaign aims to educate people facing cancer diagnoses and their loved ones about how biomarker testing may help doctors make more informed, personalized treatment decisions. It also encourages patients to discuss testing with their healthcare teams.

“Biomarkers may tell doctors the specific type of cancer present and if targeted therapies or immunotherapy might help,” Mark Socinski, MD, oncologist and Executive Medical Director of the AdventHealth Cancer Institute, told Healthline.

He explained that biomarkers are typically genes or proteins that doctors measure through blood or tissue tests. They are used to help guide treatment in numerous diseases but are especially powerful tools in many types of cancer.

It has been revealed that “They help decode why cancers behave differently, even when two people have the same cancer type,” noted Socinski. “However, while biomarker testing provides useful information, it does not guarantee a specific outcome.”.

Despite those limitations, Socinski sees promise in the shift from one-size-fits-all cancer treatment to care tailored to each patient’s specific cancer characteristics.

In a recent development, “Biomarker testing does play a critical role here, and it is important for people to be aware of the potential benefits,” Socinski stated. “It may help change the course of a person’s treatment journey.”.

Gosselaar hopes that greater awareness of biomarker testing can help people facing a cancer diagnosis feel more informed about their treatment options.

In a recent development, “A lot of the time, when a loved one or someone who has been diagnosed with cancer [it can] feel like your world is in a tailspin,” he mentioned. “I wanted to get the word out for anyone who’s going through a cancer diagnosis, or a caretaker, to know that biomarker testing is an option, because even though two cancers are similar, their tumors can act very differently and biomarker testing may help the medical expert with more personalized treatment.”.

As part of the campaign, Gosselaar took part in a commercial, something he hadn’t done since before his days on “Saved by the Bell.”.

“This was the first time that I actually had to be on set and not be a character; I had to be me talking about this very serious issue,” he remarked.

While it was a challenging experience, he stated it was also fulfilling.

“I enjoyed the process, and to be able to use my platform to be able to spread the word; it means a lot to me,” he remarked. “I’m very selective of the things that I want to attach myself to, and this seemed like the right fit.”.

He particularly enjoyed recreating Zack Morris’s signature “timeout” gesture from “Saved by the Bell,” which allowed his character to freeze time and speak directly to the camera.

“Using something from the past that was such a symbolic gesture to so many people of my generation that are now my age and possibly going through [cancer] or knowing someone who’s going through [cancer to] direct them to [this campaign], means a lot,” he mentioned.

Beyond his efforts to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing, Gosselaar is equally focused on taking care of his own health.

Industry observers note that getting quality sleep is one of his top priorities. He sleeps on a high-tech mattress that monitors sleep stages, heart rate, heart rate variability, and respiratory rate. He also uses a biometric health and fitness tracker, prioritizes healthy eating, and uses saunas and red light therapy.

In a recent development, “We do everything that we possibly can, but I’m less about longevity and more about just living a healthy lifestyle,” Gosselaar mentioned. “I want to continue doing the things that I’ve done since I was a child…without feeling held back by my health.”.

As he embraces his 50s, he noted he’d like to live a long life for his children and future grandchildren. He started taking his health seriously in his 40s after undergoing shoulder surgery.

“[It] really made me realize [that] all the damage I had done in my 20s and 30s sort of adds up later in life, and that’s probably something that I would tell the younger me… to preserve a little bit more and take [an] approach that recovery is just as crucial as the workout because I did not use my recovery very well; it was not a priority for me,” mentioned Gosselaar.

He also makes time for himself every day. He stated doing so makes him a better person and more able to care for his wife and four children.

According to recent reports, “[It’s] something that I believe in; that I need to do something for myself before I can do something for someone else. Or if I do something for someone else, then I have to equalize that by doing something for me,” he stated.

Daily physical activity also helps support his mental well-being.

In a recent development, “I need to do something where I challenge myself, and it could be as simple as a walk. It could be as simple as just getting outside and lifting something heavy [or] taking bags of groceries and taking the long way into your house,” Gosselaar said.

“Like challenging yourself with picking up things, you know, taking backpacks from the car from your kids and seeing if you can carry three in one hand…or going into the gym and spending an hour in the gym, or 30 minutes, or just moving.”.

When he’s in the sauna, he works on breathing and clearing his thoughts.

“Some people need to meditate, some people need to talk to somebody. I encourage all of that because I think all of that helps,” he stated.

“I’ve done them all. I’ve done the cold plunging, I’ve done all that stuff…some of it works, and some of it doesn’t; it’s whatever you believe in. So I just encourage people to stay healthy and move, get outside, and help other people.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.

Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.

At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.

In a recent development, on the second lap of the race, Russell, in a much faster Mercedes, passed Verstappen in the final corners coming off the Las Vegas Strip straight, then lost the lead before the first corner of the next lap. He would repeat this multiple times throughout the first half of the Grand Prix.

The race recorded a record 35 lead changes, but no one could cement a run past Verstappen.

With Verstappen slowing the field behind him, the first 10 laps of the race found the top three within one second and the top ten within less than 4.5 seconds.

Recent findings suggest that on lap 20, Sergio Perez tried to make a pick on Rafeal Camera and the Haas, and Cadillac ended up tangled in the barrier, bringing out a full safety car. In a normal race, this would’ve neutralized the race, but with everyone still running bunched up, it just sent the field all together to the pits, leading to teams double-stacking against each other.

Hamilton was the biggest loser at the pit stop, having to serve a 10-second penalty that was not yet shared with him for a battle with Norris that he thought was just.

Hamilton was kept out while everyone else pitted to clear space for Charles Leclerc and was told about his penalty.

“Ah, that’s shit. If I turned in, we would’ve crashed.”.

Recent findings suggest that under the safety car, Arvid Lindblad spun on cold tires to end his campaign for his first-ever podium. Arvid had his best starting spot of fifth for the Grand Prix and ran as high as third, while the Red Bulls on his sister team ran 1-2; he fell out of the points with the mistake.

Shortly after racing resumed, Isack Hadjar, who challenged his teammate Verstappen for the lead in the first half of the race and often put in the hardest position between the leader and the charging field, hit debris on the track and damaged his front wing. Hadjar pitted and finished outside the points as well.

With Red Bull and VCARB drivers out of contention, the door reopened for the Mercedes as Kimi Antonelli made his way into the picture following his grid drop, and Russell never left.

With two laps to go, Antonelli led Russell as the teammate fought for second; in turn 5, Russell went for the pass, overcommitted, and slid into the barrier.

Verstappen laughed on from ahead following a weekend of tension between the front-row starters.

Antonelli fell away from the lead battle on the penultimate lap with an internal glitch and would come home fourth.

In a recent development, in the mayhem, the McLarens saw their luck change at Las Vegas. Following this double disqualification while battling for the championship last year, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri walked away with a shocking first double podium of the season.

“I led for about 15 seconds, so I’m very proud,” Norris joked.

Antonelli was followed by Pierre Gasly, Franco Colapinto, Lewis Hamilton, Carlos Sainz, George Russell and Charles Leclerc in the points-paying positions.

Industry observers note that as many of Arc Raiders’ regular players predicted, the game’s first post-launch map won’t just be available for everyone, it will instead be closely tied to a community event. Breaking Fresh Ground is the name of that event, and it’s one where everyone will need to contribute in order to rebuild some old tunnels and unlock the way to Stella Montis.

The event kicks off today alongside the release of the game’s latest patch. The ask is relatively simple: players must commit Basic Materials to the project so that the tunnels can be rebuilt. This option will be available to anyone who’s played at least five rounds.

If you’ve spent any time in Arc Raiders, you’ll know that Basic Materials are things like Metal parts, Fabric, Chemicals, Rubber Parts, and Plastic Parts - most of which are easy to find in the game’s various maps.

Even beyond the ultimate goal of unlocking the fresh map, donations will also reward you with Merits, which is a new event currency, though there’s a cap on how many you can earn.

Once enough materials have been collected, the next phase of the event, Staking Our Claim, will begin, which will bring a new progression track to the game, and make Stella Montis available for players to visit.

Developer Embark describes the newly introduced environment as unlike any that we have seen in the game so far. It’s a facility carved into the northern mountains, which means it’s going to have a near-pristine look; quite the contrast with the rest of the game’s environments.

Industry observers note that stella Montis also has its own Arc enemies, loot, schematics, and other gameplay items. You can look forward to coming across the Shredder, a close-quarter Arc unit exclusive to the newly introduced map for now.

Industry observers note that then there’s The Matriarch, a somehow even larger version of the Queen. Thankfully, it will only be available under a specific map condition, so you’re in no danger of running into her randomly. The update will also introduce a upcoming legendary weapon, two new grenades, and three new mines.

In a recent development, staking Our Claim will only run until December, which is when the next stage of the game’s roadmap will kick off. Then, the Cold Snap upgrade will introduce the Flickering Flames event, the first snowfall Map Condition, and the Expedition Project voluntary wipe.

In case you’re still missing them, here’s how to find lemons and apricots, prickly pear, and olives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.

We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the newly introduced GTI hot hatch earlier this week.

Volkswagen debuted the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a newly introduced era with its first fully electric GTI.

The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, stated.

Industry observers note that after opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept shows “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.

Industry observers note that it’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.

Industry observers note that the Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.

Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, mentioned the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”.

According to recent reports, thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen said, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).

Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added new ceramic brakes to help slow it down.

The Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).

On the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a latest diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.

Inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.

The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.

Following the ID. Polo GTI, latest ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.

Sources indicate that volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

And American compact car enthusiasts drool over more unobtanium.

The company will showcase the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport concept car at the Essen Motor Show next week, starting on November 27.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm looks to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

The standard VW ID. Polo and GTI are not sold in the US, so the souped-up Clubsport variant likely won’t be either. Hopefully, VW changes its mind and proves us wrong.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello.
  • Sources indicate that in the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year.
  • See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 85206.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello. A few months ago, Ferrari unveiled the 12Cilindri Manuale, reintroducing a (simulated) six-speed manual transmission to its model lineup purely for the sake of driver involvement. And now, the Challenge Stradale badge returns to the rear engine mesh of a Prancing Horse for the first time since the 360 CS was discontinued in 2004. Simply put, it's a good year to be a sentimental Ferrarista.

Sources indicate that in the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year. Parked side by side at their reveal at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya today, we would excuse a gentleman driver for confusing the CS with his new track-only machinery.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 85206.

There have been several limited-edition, track-focused mid-engine Ferraris since the 360 Challenge Stradale—including the F430 Scuderia, 458 Speciale, and 488 Pista—but the 296 Challenge Stradale goes the furthest of all of them in emulating its racecar counterpart, both aesthetically and mechanically.

In a recent development, while previous track-centric Ferraris have been somewhat demurely styled, the 296 CS puts its aerodynamic elements on full display. The carbon-fiber rear wing, dive planes, adjustable front splitter, and vented hood are essentially a copy-paste job from the Challenge Evo, with concessions made for road legality. Up front, twin vents positioned in the hood just before the windshield channel hot air expelled from two under-hood radiators over the windshield and towards the rear of the car, reducing the aerodynamic variations caused by changing ground clearance.

Other aero features are hidden out of sight. The CS's underbody has been smoothed to better feed the rear diffuser and work with three pairs of vortex generators at the front and two at the rear to generate additional downforce. With all of the aerodynamic elements colluding, the 296 Challenge Stradale makes 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph. That's a 72-percent increase over the base 296GTB's peak figure.

In a recent development, massive changes have been made to the CS's powertrain. You won't find any orange high-voltage wiring snaking around under the glass of its mid-mounted hood like you would in a 296GTB or 296 Speciale, as the 5-kWh battery pack and rear-mounted axial-flux electric motor have been removed entirely. The twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 operates unassisted and supposedly sounds better than ever courtesy of a reworked twin-exit exhaust system.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 85206.

Sources indicate that overall firepower has decreased to 670 horsepower—149 ponies less than the standard 296GTB's. The upside is a notable decrease in mass, with Ferrari claiming that the removal of the plug-in-hybrid componentry played a major role in shedding 328 pounds from the 296GTB's dry weight. A lightened transmission flex plate, driveshaft, and timing cover were also developed to make the CS's powertrain as featherweight as possible. Without an electric motor present to fill in any thrust gaps left by turbo lag, the V-6 has been retuned to increase low-end grunt, although peak torque remains 546 pound-feet delivered at 6250 rpm.

As to be expected, yanking out an integrated powertrain system comes with some unique challenges that affect more than just the engine itself. For example, Ferrari was forced to enlarge the 296 CS's rear carbon-ceramic brake rotors and the ventilation ducts that cool them to compensate for the lack of regenerative braking. The decreased weight in the rear also shifted its weight distribution 1.5 percent to the front, which was addressed with suspension design and geometry changes.

The CS's newly developed suspension is derived directly from the 296 Challenge Evo and features semi-active dampers and a dual-spring design that improves rebound response. The result is reduced body roll, which helps the performance of the specially developed Pirelli P Zero R and P Zero Trofeo RS tires, measuring 245/35ZR-20 in the front and 305/35ZR-20 in the rear. The 20-inch forged wheels can be ordered in Matte Grigio Corsa, Matte Nero with a diamond-cut finish, or Matte Bianco Fuji.

It has been revealed that the 296 Challenge Stradale's cockpit is very similar to the one found in the 296 Speciale. While niceties like climate control and a stereo remain, carbon-fiber door panels and a lack of armrests and storage pockets are a clear indication of the CS's weight-saving mission. For true gluttons for punishment, an even further stripped interior spec is available that removes the trim from the area beneath the seats and the lower section of the carpets beneath the center console, leaving part of the chassis exposed.

According to recent reports, ferrari is adamant that the 296 CS isn't a replacement for the 296 Speciale and will not cannibalize that model's customer base, as the two are intended for different buyers. Besides being geared less towards outright track duty, the 296 Speciale is a part of Ferrari's special series, meaning that customers need to have an "existing relationship" with the brand in order to get an allocation. The 296 Challenge Stradale is a standard range model, meaning anyone can walk into a dealer and order one, existing relationship or not. Ferrari says that it wants to court new Ferrari buyers interested in experiencing the purest driving experience that the prancing horse has to offer, and the 296 CS is the first step in that direction.

U.S. pricing has not been declared, but in its home market, the 296 Challenge Stradale costs 291,000 euros, or the equivalent of about $320,000. Stateside deliveries of the fresh CS are expected to begin sometime in late 2027. As a non-Speciale model, CS production numbers aren’t limited, which presents a unique opportunity to buy a special new Ferrari without already owning one.

Early Americans spent over 10 hours making a single pumpkin pie

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1319 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s the late 1700s, and a pumpkin sits on a colonial kitchen table.
  • It seems like an absurd amount of work for dessert.
  • In a recent development, for generations, cooks solved the problem with heat and muscle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s the late 1700s, and a pumpkin sits on a colonial kitchen table. The flesh has been cooked until soft. But the hard part is still ahead. To turn the pumpkin into pie, the cook must mash it, scrape it, and force it through a sieve, separating smooth pulp from stubborn strings and fibers. There is no can of pumpkin puree. No food processor. Just the pumpkin, rudimentary kitchen tools, and a lot of elbow grease. The work could take hours, all for an eight-person dessert. An 1876 Fresh England cookbook, for example, instructed cooks to simmer pumpkin for six to eight hours, stirring frequently, before rubbing it through a colander.

It seems like an absurd amount of work for dessert. Pumpkin flesh doesn’t naturally break down into a silky puree. Cooking softens its tissues, but turning the squash into smooth filling requires additional mechanical work.

In a recent development, for generations, cooks solved the problem with heat and muscle. Eventually, factories took over the work of cooking and processing pumpkins into puree. But the solution didn’t stop there. Growers also turned to pumpkin varieties with naturally smoother, less fibrous flesh, making the job easier before the squash even reached the factory.

Recent findings suggest that pumpkin was an key food in North America long before Thanksgiving became a national holiday. Indigenous peoples cultivated and prepared the squash in many forms, and European colonists adopted pumpkins as a plentiful crop. Colonists adapted their own pie-making traditions to the abundant squash, incorporating pumpkin into sweet and savory pies. By the 17th century, recipes for pumpkin-filled pies were appearing in English cookbooks.

In 1796, the first known American cookbook, Amelia Simmons’s American Cookery, included a recipe for “Pompkin Pudding” made with cooked pumpkin, milk, eggs, and spices. Before the pumpkin could be combined with the other ingredients, the recipe called for it to be strained, separating fine pulp from tougher material.

Industry observers note that thanksgiving didn’t take shape as a national tradition until the mid-19th century. Pumpkins were harvested in the fall and could be stored through the colder months, making them a natural ingredient for a holiday associated with the autumn harvest.

It has been revealed that the story of the Pilgrims sitting down with Native Americans for the first Thanksgiving has some truth to it, too. In 1621, English colonists and members of the Wampanoag people did gather for a three-day harvest celebration. But the friendly, feel-good version passed down in schoolbooks leaves out a much more complicated history of colonialism and conflict.

It wasn’t until over two centuries later that Sarah Josepha Hale, a prominent magazine editor, campaigned for decades for a national holiday, and, in 1863, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed a national “day of Thanksgiving.” She believed a shared day of gratitude, centered on family and community, could help unite a country increasingly divided by political conflict.

According to recent reports, hale also helped popularize the foods associated with the holiday, promoting a traditional New England Thanksgiving menu through her magazine. Pumpkin pie was already a regional favorite, but as Thanksgiving spread nationally after the Civil War, the dessert became part of the broader American tradition.

According to recent reports, pumpkin pie became increasingly associated with the holiday meal during this era, drawing on its roots in Newly introduced England’s seasonal cooking traditions. Preparing it remained labor-intensive, and results varied.

Sources indicate that industrial food processing offered a solution to the labor-intensive process of making pumpkin pie. Factories could cook and mechanically break down pumpkin in large quantities, producing puree without requiring every household to repeat the tedious process. Canning transformed pumpkin from a seasonal ingredient demanding considerable preparation into a convenient product that could be stored and used when needed.

John Coupland, Ph.D., professor of food science at Penn State, describes the work involved in preparing pumpkin by hand as “astonishing.” Industrial processing made pie filling far more convenient, eliminating the need to cook, mash, and strain a pumpkin from scratch.

It also gave bakers a reliable starting point, helping make pumpkin pie more consistent and cementing its place at the Thanksgiving table.

Sources indicate that making pumpkin puree is more complicated than simply cooking the flesh until soft. Pumpkin cells are surrounded by walls containing materials such as cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin. Cooking softens the tissue, while mechanical processing breaks it into smaller particles. Together, these processes help determine the puree’s texture and moisture.

The goal is a smooth puree that is neither watery nor full of tough fibers. The pumpkin variety matters, as do the heating conditions and mechanical methods used to break down its flesh.

Recent findings suggest that modern food processing allows manufacturers to control these variables on a large scale, producing batches with similar textures and moisture levels. That predictability is especially valuable in pumpkin pie, where the filling’s consistency helps determine the finished dessert.

But the food industry found another way to improve the process: start with a pumpkin better suited to the job.

That is where Libby’s, one of the country’s largest canned-pumpkin producers, and the Dickinson pumpkin enter the story.

Sources indicate that according to Libby’s, farmer Elijah Dickinson brought special Dickinson pumpkin seeds from Kentucky to Illinois in 1835. The variety became closely associated with commercial pumpkin processing, and Libby, McNeill & Libby acquired Dickinson & Co. in 1929, strengthening the company’s connection to the crop.

Dickinson pumpkins look different from the bright orange pumpkins sold for carving (often called field pumpkins). Their tan skin matters less to processors than the dense flesh beneath it. Relatively high in solids and sugars, Dickinson pumpkins are particularly well-suited to puree.

In a recent development, many carving pumpkins, by contrast, have stringier flesh that makes them harder to process into a smooth puree. Coupland explains that they are not ideally suited to commercial food production because their fibers can be difficult to break down.

In a recent development, coupland describes Dickinson puree as having a “smooth, even texture,” adding that it means you won’t be “picking fibers out of your teeth.” Rather than trying to eliminate the stringiness of a carving pumpkin, processors can start with a variety whose natural characteristics make the job easier. The raw material itself becomes part of the technology.

Libby’s helped bring this approach into American kitchens through its canned-pumpkin business, pairing a suitable variety with industrial processing to deliver consistent puree to home bakers.

Industry observers note that interestingly, Dickinson pumpkins belong to Cucurbita moschata, a species that includes several varieties of winter squash. Many familiar carving pumpkins belong to Cucurbita pepo. Botanically, the distinction between pumpkin and squash is largely a matter of common usage rather than a strict scientific boundary. The FDA permits certain sweet, golden-fleshed squashes to be labeled as pumpkin in canned products, reflecting the longstanding overlap in how the terms are used in the food trade.

Recent findings suggest that for pumpkin pie, what matters most is the flesh inside: how it tastes, how it breaks down, and how consistently it performs. Today’s Thanksgiving cooks no longer needs to work themselves to the bone because the food industry has learned to do the work first.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe.
  • Recent findings suggest that it also didn’t wait for Brussels.
  • In a recent development, deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini announced the decision on X on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe. Italy becomes the 12th European country to allow the system, and the first of the EU’s substantial markets.

Recent findings suggest that it also didn’t wait for Brussels. The EU committee that decides on bloc-wide recognition isn’t expected to vote until December at the earliest.

In a recent development, deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini announced the decision on X on Friday. He wrote that the ministry (MIT) gave the green light after a “thorough technical feasibility check,” and that Italy is getting ahead of the EU recognition process, which he described as “still being defined.”.

Tesla Europe followed with a one-liner, “Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon,” and a video of one of its cars driving itself through Rome. There’s no firm rollout date yet.

It has been revealed that it’s still a Level 2 driver-assist system. It can steer, brake, accelerate, and handle intersections and lane changes, but the driver has to supervise at all times and stays fully responsible for the car.

Industry observers note that the Dutch vehicle authority RDW was first, approving FSD Supervised on April 10 under Article 39 of the EU type-approval regulation. Other member states can then recognize that approval nationally, one by one.

Ten did before Italy: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. Those are mostly small markets. Together with the Netherlands, they add up to about 70 million people, or roughly 15% of the EU’s population.

Italy alone has about 59 million people, so Friday’s decision nearly doubles the share of Europeans who can legally use the system, to close to 30%.

Rome’s position moved fast. In April, Senator Carlo Calenda formally asked Salvini’s ministry to prioritize the approval. On October 29, Salvini posted that he’d had a “very positive and constructive” call with Elon Musk and that Italy supported a “swift EU approval,” which read at the time as backing for an EU-level decision, not a national one. Three weeks later, Italy went national.

In a recent development, A lot changed in between. Tesla dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe after Germany’s Transport Ministry called it misleading, and cut the maximum speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit. Then on November 16, the RDW approved stricter driver monitoring, including hands on the wheel above 130 km/h. That’s the version Italy is approving.

Industry observers note that the EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) pushed the Tesla vote to December after holding only discussions in October. Bloc-wide approval needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU population.

Industry observers note that germany said in October it would back approval after Tesla agreed to the rename and the speed cap. If it follows through, Germany and the 12 approving countries would cover roughly 47% of the EU’s population.

That’s progress for Tesla, but it’s not 65%. France refused a national approval in July, and Spain hasn’t recognized the Dutch approval. Tesla needs at least one of them, plus most of the remaining holdouts.

I used FSD for five days this past week. It's impressive on controlled roads.

Even in Chill driving mode, there were still more than a few times that I had to use the Critical feedback.

To think it will ever be perfect is pure fantasy. I will never climb into a automobile that does not have steering controls.

Sources indicate that seven repairs and $10,000 on a leaky roof in two years, with no guarantees. When you factor in Musk, I'm done.

Both Carmax and OnlyUsedTesla acknowledged receiving my requests. No offers from either service 48-hours later. Guess I'm not the only one that's done with Tesla.

Recent findings suggest that this is a real win for Tesla, and for Italian owners with HW4 cars who have been paying for a feature they couldn’t use at home. Italy is Tesla’s first big European market to say yes, and it shifts momentum going into December.

But it’s pretty crazy that now Europe is going to get a safer FSD than in the US.

I bet that this will get reflected in the data, if we ever get to see it.

GLP-1s May Help Lower Diabetes, Heart Risks Better Than Standard Prevention

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 drugs are more effective in helping prevent type 2 diabetes than the commonly prescribed medication metformin, according to a fresh study.
  • Researchers said GLP-1s such as Ozempic and Mounjaro were more likely to reduce blood sugar to healthy levels in people with prediabetes and obesity.
  • They added that people prescribed GLP-1 medications had a lower risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 drugs are more effective in helping prevent type 2 diabetes than the commonly prescribed medication metformin, according to a fresh study.

Researchers said GLP-1s such as Ozempic and Mounjaro were more likely to reduce blood sugar to healthy levels in people with prediabetes and obesity.

They added that people prescribed GLP-1 medications had a lower risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.

The researchers noted that GLP-1 consumers also had a lower risk of death from any cause as well as fewer heart attacks, strokes, and heart failure events compared with metformin users.

“The great news with prediabetes is that it’s still possible to reverse the progression of the disease,” noted Vinicius de Sousa Barzon Serra, MD, a study author and research fellow in cardiovascular medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, Arizona, in a press release. “This research may add to the case for considering GLP-1 medications earlier for certain patients, rather than waiting until they develop type 2 diabetes.”.

Serra noted that metformin still remains an effective treatment for people with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes.

“This is less about replacing one medication with another and more about discussing additional options with specific patients,” he stated.

The researchers presented their findings at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago. The research has not been published yet in a peer-reviewed journal.

David Cutler, MD, a family medicine physician at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, wasn’t involved in the study, but mentioned the findings were “quite impressive.”.

“It elevates the comfort of prescribing GLP-1 drugs as a front-line treatment,” he told Healthline.

Robert Eckel, MD, a former president of the American Heart Association who was likewise not involved in the study, agrees the research provides more options for patients and prescribers.

“GLP-1s provide another option for prevention, perhaps as an add-on therapy. However, costs and access to these medications are important factors,” stated Eckel, an endocrinologist at the University of Colorado School of Medicine, in the press release.

Recent findings suggest that for their study, the researchers analyzed the medical records of 256,000 adults in the United States with prediabetes and obesity. About 76% of the subjects were women, and the average age of the participants was 52.

About half of those studied were taking GLP-1 drugs with the active ingredient semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, or dulaglutide.

The other half had been prescribed metformin, a medication used to help manage blood sugar levels in adults and some children with type 2 diabetes by decreasing glucose production in the liver, reducing glucose absorption from food, and improving the body’s insulin sensitivity.

The researchers reported that the people in the study who were taking GLP-1 drugs had a 1.5 times higher chance of reversing high blood sugar to healthy levels compared to people who were using metformin.

The researchers also noted that GLP-1 medication consumers had a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a 41% lower risk of death from any cause.

They added that GLP-1 medications were associated with 15% fewer heart attacks, 20% fewer strokes, 25% fewer cases of heart failure, and 8% fewer cases of atrial fibrillation (AFib), a common type of irregular heartbeat.

According to recent reports, the researchers cautioned that their study is observational and, therefore, cannot prove a cause-and-effect relationship. They also noted they relied on prescription records, so the frequency and dosage at which patients took their medication was not reflected.

In addition, the GLP-1 drugs were grouped together, so individual differences between medications were not considered.

It has been revealed that eckel said in the news release that the benefits for people taking GLP-1 drugs were probably mainly due to weight loss. Eckel noted that the research results open up a wide range of possibilities.

“This is an vital finding because the GLP-1 receptor agonists are commonly used today and this is a population that in the transition from prediabetes to diabetes are at increasing risk for cardiovascular disease,” Eckel noted in a taped interview alongside the study findings.

Cutler pointed out that several GLP-1 drugs also target blood sugar levels and insulin production. They could be effective in people with prediabetes who don’t have weight management issues.

Cutler noted that these people, however, might be reluctant to take GLP-1 drugs because they may not be experiencing symptoms of their prediabetes but could develop side effects with the medications.

According to recent reports, “They would not be getting any immediate benefits,” Cutler stated. He added that metformin, which was first used clinically in 1958, remains an effective alternative. “It’s been proven safe, effective, and it’s very cheap,” Cutler said.

It’s estimated that 40 million people in the United States have diabetes, with more than 90% of those cases being type 2 diabetes, a chronic condition characterized by high blood glucose levels that results from the body’s ineffective response to insulin or insufficient insulin production.

It’s also estimated that 115 million adults in the United States have prediabetes, a condition in which a person has higher-than-normal blood sugar levels but not high enough to be diagnosed as type 2 diabetes.

According to recent reports, around 5–10% of people with prediabetes develop diabetes every year. More broadly, up to 70% of people with prediabetes eventually develop diabetes.

In a recent development, medication is sometimes prescribed for people with type 2 diabetes and prediabetes. Lifestyle changes can help reverse type 2 diabetes and prediabetes, as well as prevent the progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.

Among those lifestyle modifications are:.

Cutler said the lifestyle changes needed to prevent type 2 diabetes are pretty clear.

The PopSci Proven sticker printer that cuts its own work.

Industry observers note that rated at the same 400 horsepower as the later M5 would have, this car was only just revealed by BMW’s Classic division. As a prototype, it’s quite the what-might-have-been story, although BMW probably wasn’t all that serious about producing a full M version of its luxury flagship. Instead, the V-12-powered 750iL that Pierce Brosnan pilots remotely from the back seat in 1997's Tomorrow Never Dies provided plenty of drama.

See all results for BMW 7-series for sale near 07011.

This M7 prototype would have worked just as well.

According to recent reports, besides the powertrain, a substantial part of this prototype’s appeal is just how understated it is. BMW’s M division doesn’t really do subtlety much anymore—customers want their carbon-fiber accents and M badges—but this black sedan would have flown completely under the radar in 1997. Engineers out testing it on the unrestricted autobahns must have had a heck of a time.

Sadly, like the E31-chassis, V-12-powered M8 prototype, the M7 would never make its way to a production version. Perhaps, though, that makes it all the more appealing, a secret treasure that’s been kept out of view, now finally breaking cover again. Dr. Jones might argue that it belongs in a museum.
